reviewer: human-equivalent agent review (frames sampled end-to-end + audio RMS)
method: 9 frames sampled across both scenes including 0.5s and the final second; full SRT read against the timeline; audio RMS measured per 2s; silencedetect run over the interview scene. Not a substitute for a human viewing the file in a player.

semantic_coherence.note: Scene 1 is a continuous first-person retrospective by Collins and reads in order: origin, the crew's path, the flight, the return. Scene 2 closes on Earth from the ISS, which supports 'what it felt like' rather than contradicting it.

visual_quality.note: Both sources are 320x180/320x240 archival transfers, upscaled to 1280x720. Soft, and visibly so on faces. Legible and stable throughout; no black frames, no corruption, no freeze.

composition.note: Interview is medium two-shot in a corridor with strong leading lines; subjects are off-centre with headroom. Scene 2 is a wide orbital view with the station structure to the right of frame.

motion.note: Steady handheld walk-through; no unintended motion; cuts are hard cuts.

continuity.note: Continuity inside scene 1 is driven by 11 splices, which is the standard tightened-interview look, but they are visible jump cuts rather than hidden ones. Wardrobe and identity are stable throughout.

audio.note: Real speech throughout, RMS -13 to -28 dB, no silence over 1.2s in the interview scene after dead-air removal. Scene 2 carries source ambient only.

subtitle.note: 17 cues, 97% coverage of the interview scene, no gap over 0.6s, no clipped lines, hyphenation repaired, no cue stranded on a function word. Legible white-on-black outline at 720p.

pacing.note: 22.6s interview + 14.0s B-roll = 36.7s. No dead air, no padding.

hook.note: Opens on Collins mid-gesture pointing at a wall of photographs with 'I was a young boy' — a subject and an action in the first second.

ending.note: Scene 1 closes on 'I think so.' which is a genuine conversational beat. The final frame is a thin ISS truss centred over washed-out terrain; it is the weakest image in the piece and a stronger close is available in the source.

overall.note: A real, complete, playable documentary short built from licensed archival footage with real narration, real subtitles and real evidence. The limitations are source-resolution and one weak closing frame, both recorded rather than hidden.

defects_found_and_fixed_during_review: 12.1s of dead air survived inside a single ASR segment; found by reading the SRT, fixed by splitting takes on real word-level gaps
320x180 delivery made burned text marginal; fixed by upscaling to 720p and recording that the upscale adds no detail
subtitle cues clipped at frame edge at 320px; fixed by shortening cues
BorderStyle=3 drew a partial box making text look broken; switched to outline
cues stranded clauses on function words ('...So', '...didn't'); rebalanced
first B-roll pick was a blown-out engine plume; rejected on review
second B-roll pick was a good image forced into 16:9 with pillarbox; rejected
SRT timestamps were written as bare seconds and libass rejected the whole file
defects_remaining: source resolution is 320x180/320x240; the 720p master is an upscale
final frame composition is weak (thin truss centred over flat terrain)
scene 2 has no narration; it is ambient-only B-roll
V3 semantic/composition/motion/continuity/creative were not machine-measured; they are UNKNOWN, and this human review is the record that closes them
